title: Where accidental coincidences fall, compared with a WIMP signal
caption: Regions holding 50% (filled) and 90% (outline) of each population that has a 3-fold S1 and a cS2 above 120 PE in a XENONnT-like detector, simulated with NEST. Accidental coincidences pile up in the low-cS1, low-cS2 corner, on top of a 6 GeV/c² WIMP and of ⁸B solar neutrinos, while a 50 GeV/c² WIMP mostly lies outside it along the nuclear-recoil band.
disclaimer: Illustrative toy model: recoils simulated with public software and published detector numbers, accidental coincidences from assumed isolated-S1 and isolated-S2 spectra; not data or a published template of any experiment.
s1_requirement: 3-fold PMT coincidence, no cut on the S1 area

populations.label: Accidental coincidences
populations.note: An isolated S1 paired at random with an isolated S2: both spectra fall steeply from their thresholds, so the pairs pile up in the low-cS1, low-cS2 corner. Assumed spectra.

populations.label: 6 GeV/c² WIMP
populations.note: Recoils of at most a few keV that pass the thresholds only by upward fluctuation; ⁸B solar neutrinos give nearly the same distribution.

populations.label: 50 GeV/c² WIMP
populations.note: Recoils of up to tens of keV that follow the nuclear-recoil band to large cS1, mostly away from the accidental corner.

populations.label: ⁸B solar neutrinos (CEvNS)
populations.note: Coherent scattering of ⁸B solar neutrinos on xenon nuclei, with the recoil spectrum parametrised in NEST; a signal for neutrino physics and a background for light WIMPs.

model.summary: Monte Carlo of a XENONnT-like dual-phase xenon TPC built from public software. WIMP recoil spectra come from wimprates (spin-independent, standard halo model) and the ⁸B neutrino recoil spectrum from NEST. NEST then gives the light and charge yields, their fluctuations and the detector response for a detector description filled with published XENONnT numbers (g1, g2, single-electron gain, drift field, 3-fold S1 coincidence), with the 120 PE S2 threshold of the ⁸B search and no further acceptance or selection. An accidental coincidence is an isolated S1 and an isolated S2 drawn independently from two assumed spectra that fall steeply from their thresholds, reflecting what is published qualitatively (isolated S1s are pile-ups of a few PMT hits, isolated S2s are few-electron signals); they are assumed forms, not measured spectra. Contours are highest-density regions in (cS1, log cS2), cut at the S2 threshold and at the edges of the plotted window; fraction_in_view gives the share of each population inside the window.

parameters.name: Recoil spectra, WIMPs
parameters.value: spin-independent elastic scattering on xenon for 6 and 50 GeV/c², wimprates 0.5.0 (Helm form factor)

parameters.name: Halo model
parameters.value: v0 = 238 km/s, v_esc = 544 km/s, Earth speed 252.1 km/s, local density 0.3 GeV/c²/cm³ (package defaults, which follow the recommended conventions)

parameters.name: Recoil spectrum, ⁸B neutrinos
parameters.value: CEvNS recoil spectrum on xenon as parametrised in NEST (0-5 keV, its constants for the Winter et al. neutrino spectrum)

parameters.name: Lowest recoil energy simulated
parameters.value: 0.1 keV; NEST returns no quanta for nuclear recoils below about 0.2 keV

parameters.name: Yields and fluctuations
parameters.value: NEST nuclear-recoil model (WIMPs, ⁸B, band) and beta model (electronic recoils), default parameters, at 23 V/cm

parameters.name: Drift field
parameters.value: 23 V/cm

parameters.name: g1
parameters.value: 0.151 PE/photon, entered in NEST as 0.1258 detected photons per photon; the simulation returns 0.151 PE/photon at 300 keV and 0.143 at 40 keV (single-photoelectron acceptance)

parameters.name: g2
parameters.value: 16.5 PE/electron published; NEST returns 16.50 PE/electron for the settings below (16.46 in the simulation)

parameters.name: Single-electron gain
parameters.value: 31.15 PE published; NEST returns 31.14 PE

parameters.name: Electron extraction efficiency
parameters.value: 0.53 (g2 divided by the single-electron gain); NEST returns 0.530

parameters.name: Gas-gap settings in NEST
parameters.value: gas gap 3 mm, field in the gas 6.85 kV/cm and light collection in the gas 0.154, tuned so that NEST returns the two numbers above; NEST default S2 Fano factor 3.61

parameters.name: Liquid xenon
parameters.value: 176.0 K, 1.89 bar, density 2.868 g/cm³ from NEST (published: 176.8 K, 1.89 bar; NEST treats that point as gas)

parameters.name: Geometry
parameters.value: drift length 1486 mm, liquid level 5 mm above the gate, anode 8 mm above the gate; events at the centre, no electron loss, so corrected and raw areas coincide

parameters.name: Photosensors
parameters.value: 477 PMTs; double-photoelectron probability 0.2 and single-photoelectron resolution 0.35 (typical R11410 values); channel threshold 0.13 PE; single-photoelectron acceptance 0.912
parameters.source: 0 and 1; double-photoelectron probability and resolution assumed

parameters.name: S1 requirement
parameters.value: 3-fold coincidence with NEST's rule: at least 3 photons counted above the channel threshold, in different PMTs; no cut on the S1 area

parameters.name: S2 threshold
parameters.value: cS2 of at least 120 PE

parameters.name: Electronic-recoil band
parameters.value: flat spectrum, 0-10 keV, NEST beta model

parameters.name: Nuclear-recoil median
parameters.value: flat spectrum, 0.1-40 keV, NEST nuclear-recoil model

parameters.name: Isolated-S1 spectrum (accidentals)
parameters.value: 3 counted photons plus a geometric excess of mean 1.2; 3% flat tail from 3 to 40; areas from the same single- and double-photoelectron response

parameters.name: Isolated-S2 spectrum (accidentals)
parameters.value: power law n^-2 in extracted electrons, n = 2 to 400, each pulse built by NEST's S2 routine, cut at 120 PE. The accidental background is flat across the three cS2 bins of the published ⁸B search, which were chosen to hold equal numbers of accidentals; their edges (about 156 and 233 PE up to 500 PE in SR1, 166 and 248 PE in SR0) imply a spectrum close to cS2^-2 after all selections. Used beyond 500 PE as an extrapolation
parameters.source: read from Fig. 2 of ref. 1; approximate

parameters.name: Simulated events
parameters.value: 300000 above thresholds per population; contours from a histogram smoothed by 0.5 PE and 0.05 dex
